Virtual assistant for marketing agencies

A marketing agency virtual assistant tracks campaign briefs, creative assets, editorial approvals and releases across client accounts.

A virtual assistant for creative agencies can organise drafts, collect feedback and keep approved assets beside the campaign schedule. The account lead can see which version is ready and where an approval is still holding up a release.

We can also prepare posts, check links and record published URLs across the channels you approve. Your team decides when a campaign goes live and handles changes to client messaging.

Keep two client releases on the same calendar

Your marketing agency virtual assistant can manage overlapping client dates. Your virtual assistant for creative agencies should record which approval affects each scheduled release.

An agency is preparing a landing page for one client and an editorial release for another. Both need the same designer’s time. A useful delivery handoff makes the conflict visible without mixing accounts, approvals or unpublished material.

  1. 01

    Separate the briefs before grouping the work

    Record each client’s objective, due date and final approver in its own workspace. Link the shared design dependency on the internal calendar. Share only the level of cross-account detail that the delivery team is authorised to see.

  2. 02

    Identify the decision that unblocks the calendar

    Show what can proceed using approved assets and what depends on the designer. Give the account leads two realistic sequencing options and note which deadline would move under each. Ask the priority owner to decide.

  3. 03

    Deliver and preserve the approval trail

    Keep preview links and feedback attached to the correct brief. Once the final version is approved, schedule it and record the release link. Send the account lead a short summary of published work and items still waiting.

Prepare the inputs and rules.

A virtual assistant for marketing agencies needs an approved example from each client. Your marketing agency virtual assistant should check versions before moving an asset into production.

Account boundaries

Identify separate folders, credentials and review channels for each client or publication. Explain how a shared resource can be scheduled without exposing another account’s material.

Release criteria

Define which items require a preview, source checks or image clearance. Confirm which person signs off on the version that will be published.

Calendar ownership

Agree who resolves conflicts, how urgent work is flagged and whether a missed decision should delay publication. Give the marketing agency virtual assistant a clear route to reach that owner.

Decide what happens when the normal rule fails.

Your virtual assistant for creative agencies should flag contradictory feedback. Your marketing agency virtual assistant needs a confirmed decision before replacing approved work.

A client sends feedback to the wrong channel

Record it in the correct review thread and confirm it applies to the current draft. Ask the account lead to check any conflicting instruction.

A required asset has not cleared review

Mark the item blocked and show the effect on the calendar. Offer an approved substitute only when the client or editorial lead can sign off.

Two deadlines are both described as urgent

List the dependencies and the effect of moving either item. Ask the priority owner to decide before changing dates.

Check the work against the original brief.

Review your marketing agency virtual assistant against client commitments. A virtual assistant for marketing agencies can show where missing approval affected a delivery date.

Version control

Pick one released item per account and trace it from brief to final approval and live link. Note where competing files made the reviewed version unclear.

Delivery visibility

Check whether the status report distinguishes work that is scheduled, ready for review and blocked. Give each open item an owner and next action.

Client separation

Review a sample of links, assets and folders. Confirm that each was shared through the account’s agreed channel with the expected access.

Leave a record the next person can use.

Your virtual assistant for creative agencies should leave assets, feedback and dates together. Your marketing agency virtual assistant should preserve the latest client decision.

Marketing agency virtual assistant production setup

Ask for the approved brief, client contact and date for the first review. Record which asset version and channel are in scope, especially when two clients have similar work due in the same week.

Virtual assistant for marketing agencies review tracking

Frequently Asked Questions

Ask how your virtual assistant for creative agencies handles client access. Your marketing agency virtual assistant should keep account information and review records in the correct workspace.

Can one workflow cover several client accounts?

Use a shared process for status and deadlines, with separate folders, access and approval rules for each account.

What happens when urgent work interrupts the calendar?

Flag the work that would move, then let the account or editorial lead confirm the new priority before changing deadlines.

What needs approval before content is scheduled?

Give your marketing agency virtual assistant the approved copy, asset version, channel and release date. Identify the reviewer who can confirm a change so the team can check the exact item before it is scheduled.

Can support coordinate work across several channels?

A virtual assistant for marketing agencies can maintain a shared calendar linking the approved assets, review dates and destinations. Agree channel-specific checks and note which releases depend on the same page or client approval.

How do we keep client work separate?

A virtual assistant for creative agencies should use the approved workspace and access rules for each account. Keep source assets, client feedback and approval records in the correct folders while sharing only the status information needed for coordination.

What happens if reviewers give conflicting feedback?

Record both instructions and ask the named decision owner which version should be used. Keep the affected item visible in the review queue and check any scheduled releases that depend on the same decision.
